Servicing: statements, changes, prepayment and foreclosure

After this lesson you can:
  • List the standard servicing events and their evidence
  • Explain part-prepayment options and foreclosure quotes
  • Describe closure done right: NOC, releases, registry and bureau updates

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page
  1. The quiet majority of the lifecycle
  2. Paying early: prepayment and foreclosure
  3. Closure is a checklist, not an event
  4. Regulatory anchors

1. The quiet majority of the lifecycle

Most of a loan's life is servicing: statements (periodic and on-demand), interest certificates for tax season, profile changes (address, contact, bank account — each verified, some maker-checked), due-date changes, hardship requests, and the rate-reset ritual from the schedules lesson. Every borrower-facing communication leaves delivery evidence, in the borrower's preferred language where configured.

LoanOS's borrower portal surfaces the account view — balance, next due, schedule, documents, grievance — so servicing requests originate from an authenticated, attributable channel.

2. Paying early: prepayment and foreclosure

Part-prepayment reduces principal mid-tenor, and the borrower chooses the effect: lower EMI (same tenor) or shorter tenor (same EMI) — the latter usually saves more interest. The system re-amortises and issues a new schedule version with communication.

Foreclosure closes the loan early: the borrower requests a foreclosure quote — outstanding principal + accrued interest to the payoff date + permitted charges — valid for a stated window.

Charge rules are borrower-protective: RBI prohibits foreclosure charges on floating-rate loans to individuals for non-business purposes, and every charge must trace to the KFS.

Payoff, closure and the paper trail follow.

3. Closure is a checklist, not an event

A loan ends properly only when:

  1. Dues are zero (scheduled completion, foreclosure or settlement).
  2. The NOC / no-dues certificate is issued.
  3. Mandates are cancelled.
  4. For secured loans: original documents returned within the required timeline and the CERSAI security-interest satisfaction is filed (registry timelines apply; delays carry compensation duties and grievance exposure).
  5. The CIC closure update goes out so the borrower's bureau file shows the loan closed.

Skipping step 4 or 5 is the classic post-closure harm: a borrower who repaid in full but whose bureau report still shows the loan open, or whose property papers are lost in a branch. Both are grievance magnets with regulatory teeth.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-DL-2025 — Servicing conduct, communication evidence and borrower protections.
  • RBI-CIR-2025 — Closure must reach the CICs promptly; correction clocks and compensation protect the borrower.
  • CERSAI-CKYC — Security-interest satisfaction at closure for secured loans.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Capability SRV-002 — Periodic and on-demand statements.
  • Capability LMS-013 — Part-prepayment with EMI/tenure choice.
  • Capability LMS-014 — Foreclosure quote, charge policy, payoff and closure.
  • Capability CLS-009 — NOC / no-dues certificate.
  • Capability CLS-012 — CIC closure update and borrower confirmation.
  • App surface /t/{tenantId}/portal/ — Borrower portal (tenant-scoped): schedule, statements, documents, grievance.

Retrieval practice

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. A borrower part-prepays ₹2 lakh and wants maximum interest savings. Which option?

  1. Reduce EMI, keep tenor
  2. Reduce tenor, keep EMI
  3. Split half and half
  4. Hold as advance EMI
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. Keeping the EMI constant against a lower principal shortens the tenor and cuts total interest more than lowering the instalment.

2. A repaid borrower's bureau report still shows the loan open after months. Which duty failed?

  1. KYC refresh
  2. The CIC closure update
  3. Mandate cancellation
  4. NOC printing
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. Closure must flow to the CICs; a stale open status is exactly the harm the correction clocks and compensation rules target.
